known_analogues: Recurrence for polynomial sequences of degree 3
proof_mechanisms: 1. For a cubic polynomial p(n), the third forward difference is constant: Δ³p = constant.
2. This translates to recurrence f(n) = 3f(n-1) - 3f(n-2) + f(n-3) + 2.

4. Note: standard linear_recurrence format may not support constant offset; this may need representation as order-4 recurrence with coefficients [4,-6,4,-1] and seeds [0,1,5,14] where the characteristic root 1 absorbs the constant.
claim.statement: Cross-domain synthesis combining parent_7's polynomial identity with recurrence theory. A degree-3 polynomial always satisfies an order-4 homogeneous linear recurrence with coefficients from binomial(4,k)*(-1)^k. Using seeds f(0)=0, f(1)=1, f(2)=5, f(3)=14, the recurrence f(n)=4f(n-1)-6f(n-2)+4f(n-3)-f(n-4) should hold exactly.
